## Maths

Inline: the BCS gap parameter $\Delta_{\mathbf k}$ is determined
self-consistently. Display, with a reference tag:

$$
\Delta_{\mathbf k} = -\sum_{\mathbf k'} V_{\mathbf k \mathbf k'}\,
\frac{\Delta_{\mathbf k'}}{2 E_{\mathbf k'}}
\tanh\!\left( \frac{E_{\mathbf k'}}{2 k_B T} \right)
$$ {#eq-gap}

with $E_{\mathbf k} = \sqrt{\xi_{\mathbf k}^2 + |\Delta_{\mathbf k}|^2}$.
@eq-gap is the standard gap equation; solving it is where the numerics start.

Aligned multi-line derivations work as expected:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathcal{H}_{\mathrm{BdG}}
  &= \sum_{\mathbf k} \begin{pmatrix} c^\dagger_{\mathbf k\uparrow} & c_{-\mathbf k\downarrow}\end{pmatrix}
     \begin{pmatrix} \xi_{\mathbf k} & \Delta_{\mathbf k} \\ \Delta^*_{\mathbf k} & -\xi_{\mathbf k}\end{pmatrix}
     \begin{pmatrix} c_{\mathbf k\uparrow} \\ c^\dagger_{-\mathbf k\downarrow}\end{pmatrix} \\
  &= \sum_{\mathbf k} E_{\mathbf k}\left( \gamma^\dagger_{\mathbf k\uparrow}\gamma_{\mathbf k\uparrow}
     + \gamma^\dagger_{\mathbf k\downarrow}\gamma_{\mathbf k\downarrow} \right) + \mathrm{const.}
\end{aligned}
$$

## Code

Static code — always renders, no Python needed:

```python
import numpy as np

def gap_rhs(delta, xi, V, T, kB=8.617333e-5):
    E = np.sqrt(xi**2 + np.abs(delta) ** 2)
    return -(V @ (delta / (2 * E) * np.tanh(E / (2 * kB * T))))
```

To *execute* code and embed its output, use `{python}` instead of `python` in
the fence. That needs Jupyter installed — see the repo `README.md`.
